slides.title: AI Robot and Regular Robot
slides.text:
AI Robot and Regular Robot
  •  The basic difference between an AI robot and a
   more regular robot is the
     –  ability of the robot and its software to make decisions
     – and to learn and adapt to its environment based on
        data from its sensors.
  •  Thus, we are leaving the world of pre-coded robot
    design behind.
  •  Instead of programming all of the robot’s
    behaviors in advance,
     – the robot software, will learn from the examples
      we provide, or from interacting with the outside world.

slides.title: The Turing Test
slides.text:
The Turing Test
  •  A human judge converses (via text) with a human and a machine. If the judge
    cannot reliably tell which is which, the machine passes.
  •  The Turing test was proposed by Alan Turing in 1950 in a paper titled
    "Computing Machinery and Intelligence."
  •  Components required:
    – Natural Language Processing
    – Knowledge Representation
    – Automated Reasoning
    – Machine Learning
  •  No machine has fully passed an unrestricted Turing
     Test.
  •  CAPTCHA is an inverse Turing Test.



                                                                                                             8

slides.title: Machine Learning
slides.text:
Machine Learning

    "A computer program is said to learn from experience E with respect to
    some class of tasks T and performance measure P, if its performance at tasks
      in T, as measured by P, improves with experience E." — Tom Mitchell, 1997

    Traditional Programming              Machine Learning

    Rules + Data → Output                 Data + Output → Rules
    Explicit human-written logic.             Algorithm discovers patterns.
    Fragile when rules are complex.           Scales to complex problems.
      IF speed > 50 AND obstacle_dist           model.fit(sensor_data, actions)
    < 2 THEN brake()

    Types: Supervised, Unsupervised & Reinforcement Learning

slides.title: Neural Network Architecture
slides.text:
Neural Network Architecture
                                                   Transformers
•  Feed-forward Neural Network (FNN)                   •  Replaced RNNs for sequence
    – No loops                                             modelling.
    –  Not good for sequential data                             •  Foundation of all modern LLMs
•  Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)                  and many robot learning
    –  Useful in context                                     systems.
    – Memory, they affect future o/p                           •  Calculate attention score
    –  For language translation, speech recognition.
    – Bad for long term memory so LSTM is used.
•  Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)
    –  Exploit the spatial structure in images through local
        connectivity and parameter sharing.
    –  Looks at small patch of image at a time and thus reduce
       input size.
    – Used in object classification, video analysis

slides.title: 3D Perception: LiDAR & Point Clouds
slides.text:
3D Perception: LiDAR & Point Clouds

  Point Cloud Processing

  •  LiDAR sensors produce point clouds:
        •  Unordered sets of (x,y,z) 3D points.
        •  Unlike images, point clouds lack grid structure —
         requiring special neural network architectures.
  •  PointNet (2017):
        •  process each point independently,
        •  then aggregate with symmetric function (max-pool).
        •  Handles permutation invariance.





                                                                                                          23

  Robots must understand and generate natural language to collaborate with humans —
  from simple pick-and-place commands to complex multi-step task instructions.

   Whisper, wav2vec 2.0, DeepSpeech.           BERT, RoBERTa, GPT fine-tuning.
   Acoustic model + language model.             Intent classification + slot filling.
   Robot: voice command interpretation.         Grounding: connect language to percepts.
   Online streaming with VAD.                  Ambiguity resolution via context.

                                                 Track conversation state.  Map language to robot actions.
                                                       Clarification questions when ambiguous.   SayScan: LLM + value functions.

slides.title: AI Ethics & Responsible AI
slides.text:
AI Ethics & Responsible AI

     With great capability comes great responsibility. AI-powered robots make decisions that affect human safety,
      fairness, and privacy — ethics must be designed in from the start.

    Algorithmic Bias                                   Privacy
                                                                            •   Vision AI collects sensitive data.     •   Training data reflects societal biases.
                                                                            •   On-device inference avoids cloud exposure.     •   Facial recognition disparities across demographics.
                                                                            •   Federated learning for privacy-preserving robot     •   Grasp models biased toward common objects.
                                                                            training.
    Safety & Reliability                       Human Autonomy
                                                                            •   Robots should augment, not replace human
      •   Robot failures can cause physical harm.
                                                                decision-making in high-stakes situations.
      •   Fail-safe design: always default to safe state
                                                                            •   Human-in-the-loop for critical actions.

     Explainable AI(XAI)
      •  Humans must understand why robots act.
      •   Black-box models problematic in medical and
          legal robot deployment contexts.




                                                                                                          39
